clue.text: Soldiers kept in trim in service? True

indicators.note: in places the soldiers-in-trim unit inside the word for a service

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis

indicators.note: kept in says the soldiers sit inside the word for trim

parts.note: to trim is to cut
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A question about whether troops are kept fit while serving, answered with a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts RA inside CUT to make CURAT; the second 'in' puts that inside ACE, between AC and E. 'In trim' reads as fit, but trim is CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is correct and exact, as a true statement is.

clue.text: Creative work disc contains is noble

indicators.note: contains says the art-and-disc run holds the word is within it

parts.note: art is creative work
O is disc-shaped, a circle

explanation.surface: A claim that a piece of art on a record is a noble thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts IS inside ARTO (ART plus O), between AR and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is short for an aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Person making clothing more comfortable around stomach

indicators.note: around says the comparative wraps about the word for belly

parts.note: cosier means more comfortable
tum is a colloquial word for the stomach

explanation.surface: Describes a tailor who makes garments roomier around the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts TUM inside COSIER, after COS.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, garments for the stage or fancy dress.

clue.text: Screen repeat about Queen, head of state

indicators.note: about says the word for repeat goes round the royal abbreviation

parts.note: to redo is to do again, repeat
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of state

explanation.surface: A screen repeating something about the Queen as head of state, like a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ER inside REDO after its R, making REREDO; 'head of' adds S from state.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Stretch of dramatically rising river

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
a stretch of a word is a run of its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A river climbing steeply along a stretch of its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch of' takes RAMAT from inside dRAMATically; 'rising' turns it round. The Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is an English river forming most of the Devon-Cornwall border.

clue.text: Programme info's written in the first person, mostly

indicators.note: written in says the information goes inside the shortened name
mostly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Adam was the first person in the Bible
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A programme document written as first-person information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ADAM to ADA; 'written in' puts GEN inside it. 'The first person' looks grammatical (I) but is Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or plan.

clue.text: Irritating grid

explanation.surface: A complaint that a grid of some kind is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Grating means annoying, harsh to the ear; a grating is also a framework of bars, a grille.

clue.text: Wide-eyed one enthralled by central space in church

indicators.note: enthralled by says the numeral is held inside the church area

parts.note: the nave is the main central body of a church
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone gazing in wonder, captivated in the middle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' puts I inside NAVE, after NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and credulous, like someone wide-eyed.

clue.text: Sad tale about end of ended thus

annotationWithheld.why: Sad tale about end of ended thus: an anagram of TALE with RE (about) and D (end of ended) leaves an N unaccounted for; the clue looks garbled in the OCR and no reprint was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Sad tale about end of ended thus

clue.text: National border held by articles to be object of loathing

indicators.note: held by says the pair of words go inside the two articles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article; two of them are taken
a is the indefinite article; two of them are taken
Nat. is a standard abbreviation for national
a hem is the edge or border of cloth

explanation.surface: A national border policed by rules that make it hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts NATHEM between A and A; 'articles' is plural, so it supplies both.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is something or someone intensely detested.

clue.text: Player batting in last Test miserably without spirit

parts.note: a cricket side batting is in

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters go round the drink
miserably says the words in, last, Test are rearranged

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A cricketer batting badly in the final Test, lacking any fighting spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' turns IN LAST TEST into STENTALIST; 'without' (outside) puts it around RUM after ST. Batting cricketers are said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a musician who plays an instrument, a player.

clue.text: Roar hard in backing revolutionary crackpot

indicators.note: in puts the pencil grade inside the turned-round pair
backing means the run of words is read in reverse

parts.note: red means a revolutionary, a communist
a nut is a crackpot, a crazy person
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Loud shouting in support of a revolutionary eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses REDNUT to TUNDER; 'in' puts H after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is a loud rumbling roar, and to thunder is to roar.

clue.text: Error, item to be amended (or deleted) in galley

indicators.note: to be amended says the letters of error and item are reworked
deleted says the letters of or are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: An editor's note: an error and an item to be corrected or cut in a printer's galley proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool ERROR and ITEM, remove O and R ('or deleted'), and rearrange the rest. 'Galley' suggests a proof, but it is the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Put off date to release entertaining commercial

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting, so the advertisement goes inside

parts.note: to issue is to release
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Postponing a launch date because an amusing advert is being released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts AD inside ISSUE, after ISSU; D goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade is to deter, to talk someone out of doing something.

clue.text: Roguish plan involves bit of skulduggery? That's an old-fashioned term

parts.note: arch means mischievous, roguish

indicators.note: involves says the aim holds the letter within it

parts.note: an aim is a plan or intention

indicators.note: bit of picks out the first letter of skulduggery

explanation.surface: A scheming rogue's plot involving foul play, described in quaint language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives S, and 'involves' puts it inside AIM after AI; ARCH goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is a word or expression no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: In expressing affection, blunder

indicators.note: In says the letters run inside the words expressing affection

explanation.surface: A clumsy mistake made while trying to show fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in expressinG AFFEction, across the word join.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, an embarrassing slip.

clue.text: Waver, being tense about climbing inside chimney

indicators.note: inside says the turned pair goes within the chimney word

parts.note: a flue is a chimney duct

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters go upwards, reversed

parts.note: taut means tense
c. is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating nervously while clambering up a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses TAUTC to CTUAT; 'inside' puts it inside FLUE after FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluctuate is to vary or rise and fall irregularly, to waver.

clue.text: Sort of thing that survives in backstreets and mews?

definitions.text: Sort of thing that survives in backstreets and mews?

parts.words: Sort of thing that survives in backstreets and mews?
parts.note: backstreets and mews read as narrow lanes, but mews is also the cry of a feline living rough in such lanes

explanation.surface: Something that endures in the back alleys and mews of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a small backstreet of converted stables; it also means the sounds a cat makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray town cat that lives rough in lanes and makes mewing sounds.

clue.text: Sensational line Unionist delivered

parts.note: rid in the sense of freed, delivered from

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician delivers a dramatic line.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivered as in delivered from evil: rid, freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking and sensational, as in lurid headlines.

clue.text: Point of view Democrat after Democrat presented enticingly

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes behind the other one

parts.note: an angle is a point of view, a slant

explanation.surface: One Democrat's viewpoint offered temptingly after another Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGLE D comes after D, giving D ANGLE D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangled means held out as a lure or temptation.

clue.text: Tribe to leave city in uproar

parts.note: a clan is a tribe
to go is to leave
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A tribe deserting a city amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a loud ringing din, a clamour.

clue.text: Virtuous man a prisoner set up and deceived

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a lag is a convict, a prisoner
had means tricked, deceived

explanation.surface: A good man and a convict framed and fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses ALAG to GALA; HAD follows. 'Set up' also reads as framed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest of Arthur's knights, stands for a chivalrous, virtuous man.

clue.text: Suit that's beginning to be comprehended by judges

indicators.note: comprehended by in the sense of included, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a judge hears a case

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of that's

explanation.surface: A lawsuit that judges are starting to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' gives T from that's; 'comprehended by' puts it inside HEARS after HEAR. Suit looks legal, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Answer, after shuffling of notes, I state

indicators.note: after says the answer letter comes behind the mixed letters
shuffling of says the letters of notes and I are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone stating an answer after rearranging their notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffling of' turns NOTES I into ESTONI; A comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Have experience of discrimination

explanation.surface: A person who knows prejudice firsthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to experience it briefly; taste is also discernment, good judgement in style.

clue.text: Whitish gallery lacking a range of colours

parts.note: pale means whitish

indicators.note: lacking says the gallery name loses the letter

parts.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: A drab gallery missing its colourful exhibits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' removes the A of TATE to leave TTE. The Tate is Britain's national art gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the range of colours an artist uses.

clue.text: Enclose centimes, European coins

parts.note: to pen is to enclose
c. is short for centimes

explanation.surface: Putting centimes in an envelope with other European money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are small British coins, plural of penny.

clue.text: Daydreams tantalise, riches being involved

indicators.note: being involved in the sense of tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fantasies that tease the mind with dreams of wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being involved' (tangled) rearranges TANTALISE RICHES into the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in the air are idle fantasies, impractical dreams.

clue.text: Aim to fill crack in

indicators.note: to fill says the goal goes inside the word for crack

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, a try
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Trying to plug a gap in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' puts END inside TRY after TR. 'In' is the definition: fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In and trendy both mean fashionable, currently popular.

clue.text: Pointers, by end of process, not required

parts.note: needles are pointers on dials

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of process

explanation.surface: Gauges made unnecessary at the end of a procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, not needed.
